steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Can we talk specifics, now that it's just the two of us? You might have fooled the others, but you can't fool me.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: So that was enough to fool the others.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: What did Kuznetsov do to you? Did he put any holes in you? Let me see—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Ever since that purification operation in December, everybody had tons of questions for me whenever they ran into me on the training grounds, but no one said anything today.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Is it because optimism is our nature? Does nothing else matter?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Because they believe in you, of course! The Ataman who lights the way, the war caster of legend, the great leader of the Volniki, who reap enemies like mossoat...

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Who would they believe in, if not you?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Wow, keep going, any other titles I haven't heard of?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: —But if you ask me, I would say that foolishness is our nature.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Foolish enough to not remember old grudges, foolish enough to survive, foolish enough that people in power won't suspect that we might get back at them.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I'm glad Sirka isn't here to hear it.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: I'm your second-in-command now. Stop talking about our noble lady every opportunity you get.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Well, you don't like it when I bring up Pavel.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: He's been gone three years, he's probably hit it big again somewhere else. He doesn't need us to reminisce about him.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: In Baba's name, man was born to be a quartermaster. He can fill his pockets wherever he goes. If it wasn't for Oripathy...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: He never wrote back.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Were you robbing Messengers again?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Come on, you knew where I was these past two days, Gospodin Oleg, how would I find the time?

spans.text: Come on, you knew where I was these past two days,
Oleg, how would I find the time?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Finally getting back on topic? Now talk. What happened?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: What I said, basically.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: What about the part that's not 'basic'?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Not basic, eh... you were there when I killed Basmanov, weren't you?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: You remember what he said to me?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...Surrender to Kuznetsov. That's all he wants.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Stop resisting, Basmanov. It was sheer madness to commit mutiny on the front lines, not to mention your second-in-command was leaking all your plans—

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: I don't blame him.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: I don't blame him. I don't blame anyone...

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: I just blame myself for not seeing the truth sooner.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: What truth? The obvious truth that you can't win?

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: The truth that the flames have already burned away houses and clothes, and will soon reach the skin and the flesh beneath... we should have awakened sooner.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: What are you talking about—

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: I don't blame you, truly. I knew it was you who came, when even Private Vyacheslav made it to the bridge alive to deliver the news.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: The Special Tactics Formation... the isolated, expendable, fickle executioners, the free Volniki who are never truly free—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: All I know is that the arrival of Sechin means you won't even get a court martial.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: Yet you're giving me a chance to escape, just like how you let the miners go.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: On the surface, you're just doing everything Kuznetsov told you to do. Yet even now, you're trying to give me a way out, against his wishes.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: The stalemate continues. Kuznetsov needs every soldier he can get. He will forgive, if you surrender.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: Do you know the name Yakov Petrov, Major?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: What I shame.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: It's only now that I realize that there was someone who saw that the house was burning, except no one was listening to him, and called him a madman.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: That is what they will call me. Oczip Basmanov the traitor, disciple of Yakov Petrov.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: That's all I have to say, Major. I'm not surrendering. You do what you must.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: I only hope that your blade will always remember who you are.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Thirty-two klicks until the front, sir. We're seven hundred and fifty-one klicks from Zelgrad.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: ETA is five hours for the former and seven days for the latter.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Good work.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Oleg will relieve you in half an hour.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: I can go on—

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: No you can't. Go to bed.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: This kid was on duty all day in the control room while you were away. He only took a two-hour break before coming back. Won't listen to me at all.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: I was just worried!

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Stop worrying. If thinking about things ever did any good, I would have prayed to Baba for a bolt of thunder to smite Kuznetsov.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Now get out of here, I'll be checking the quarters in two hours.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Good, looks like life will go on, if anything happens to me.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Do you need your eyes checked? Did you see any of them listen to what I say?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: They will when I'm gone. You're more of a leader than I am. It was a wise move to move you out of logistics—

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: It was because I made good pies and didn't let you take extra ones, wasn't it?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Well, that's part of it.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: I knew you were out for vengeance.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Come on, don't say that—

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: You're still thinking about what Basmanov said.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: —Huh?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Maybe his ramblings made sense in his own mind, but that last thing he said was clearly a taunt.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: You trust your blade more than you trust anyone else, don't you?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Now that's unfair, of course I trust you guys more.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Idi v'banyu. We all know that they call us Volniki the free folk because we have the freedom to come together or part ways as we please—

spans.text: . We all know that they call us Volniki the free folk because we have the freedom to come together or part ways as we please—

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: So, the only things we can and must trust is ourselves and our swords.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Is that a sword, anyway? Or an Arts unit? What IS it?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Never mind. Anyway, it will always know you, and it will never kill you. That's all that matters.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Oleg.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: You like to talk about Baba. Do you know who she is, or what she looks like?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: No idea. She might be Kuranta, or Liberi, or Elafia, but she couldn't be Ursus.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: All old stories that we tell to pass the time. We need stories and song to bring us together. Isn't that what your precious Sirka always said?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...'Our Baba put a glass house upon the legs of a fowlbeast'...

a.text: Our Baba put a glass house upon the legs of a fowlbeast.
Not to move from place to place like us, but so that she could turn around and shut people out at any time.
She never asks what you want, but asks:
She takes your burdenbeast, your sword and bow, the wealth that you traded blood for;
Even the victory that made your mother proudest.
Our ancestors called her an evil witch, but they learned when they grew old—
She was simply collecting on death's behalf.
If one has nothing left to pay:
Their sword thrice-broken, their siblings all buried upon different battlefields, and with no strength left to even hate—
She no longer blocks the way, but turns her hut around, and reveals the path without echoes.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: 'The last thing she said to us was...'

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: 'I can protect you no longer.'

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: You can't carry a tune, but you remember the words well.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Sirka sang it for me a lot.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Alright, you can stop—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I often wonder, if there comes a day when even the all-powerful Baba can no longer protect us...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: How far will we go to survive?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Message from central command.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Put it through.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: I see you've left the base.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: An astute observation, sir.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You should be reporting your position and status every two hours, Major Razin.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: A report every two hours is impractical. Should I explain the reason in detail?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Do not waste time on long-range communications. Report on your progress.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Well, as you know, the Volnov has left the base and is currently approaching the front lines. Assuming we do not need to linger near the front lines and observe the situation—

spans.text: has left the base and is currently approaching the front lines. Assuming we do not need to linger near the front lines and observe the situation—

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: There's no need. Proceed directly.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Even if it might cause the Second Army to attack?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: I said, it is not your concern. What you should be concerned with is getting your men near the satellite city before you run out of power.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: There's no time for you to stop, according to my estimations. The Volnov must arrive at the designated location in three days and complete the mission in conjunction with another unit.

spans.text: There's no time for you to stop, according to my estimations. The
must arrive at the designated location in three days and complete the mission in conjunction with another unit.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I don't know anything about any other unit.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Now you do.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Now, what is the current progress of the Volnov?

spans.text: Now, what is the current progress of the

steps.text: Scioppa takes his time glancing at the control panel before answering.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Accelerating steadily. I can't give you an accurate figure, but it will eventually reach a figure that will allow us to arrive by the ETA.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Is that so...?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Then I hope that central command will not have to initiate the next communication.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Why did you lie to him? How long can we keep this up?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: In order to survive, we must first solve our most pressing problem.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Give the Second Army enough time to react, then pray that Kuznetsov's 'guarantee' pays off before we're blown to smithereens.
Hiding by yourself again, my brother Fedya?
Why aren't you with Mother?

a.text: I... like your apple tree. Besides—I don't want to stay there anymore...
That smell is everywhere in the room... I don't want to go back!

steps.text: What smell? The smell of disinfectants, of bitter almond?
The smell is from things that help Mother. I put bitter almond fragrance in my room to stop myself from coughing, and to relieve the pain...
You know that.
Because those people in black won't let me go in anymore.
They don't even want me to come near you.
She picks a low-hanging fruit and puts it in the boy's hand.
The fruit is red like agate, like the culmination of the sun of countless summers at the palace, summers that he had forgotten.
He no longer sees the red corridor in the glass palace, only the rays of the sun shining through the leaves and branches like broken glass, and the cool apple upon his palm.
He hears only the sweet, glass-like voice in his ear.
But I'll pay them no heed.
You're my only brother. Nothing can break our bonds of blood.
I'll find you.
Fedya... Fedya!
*cough* *cough* Thank goodness, you're still here.
Listen, I know you don't want to go, but you must. Go with them to Mother's funeral. Do you understand?
I can't be there, but you can...
Come, let me sort your tie out. Your pants are dirty. Did you trip again? You're always so clumsy—
Now, go.
I'll wait for you... under the apple tree.
Yes, my brave Fedya. Do not be afraid, though some may try to confuse and control you, for you are stronger than them all.
You will hear the most sincere voice, the voice of me calling to you.
And I will be here, waiting for you.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...The summer palace? Why am I dreaming about something from so long ago...?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The one in the dream... a sister?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: But I have no siblings...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Argh—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: (The headaches are getting more frequent.)

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: (Ever since I came back from Katorga...)

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty, I bring the latest progress report on the citizen's forum.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Good timing. Saves me from thinking too much.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You look tired.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Strange, isn't it... I had a dream about the summer palace, which I have not seen in many years.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: There's a beautiful apple orchard nearby. It'll be a good place to recuperate, if you feel the need.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: ...Apple orchard?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Never mind, it's not important—what's the progress?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Most nobles who were already on our side are inclined to continue, following the Katorga Incident.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: They have quickly accepted the decision to trial the citizen's forum, and a few of them are even willing to divert tax funds to establish similar pilot programs in their territories.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I believe it's a good start.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What's the catch?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I'm sure Your Imperial Majesty understands...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: The Winter Emergency Resource Allocation Act will not convince the conservatives of the State Council just because it passed the citizen's forum.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: It's not just the conservatives. No aristocrat will willingly give up their own profits, much less allow the council to dictate what little remains of the nation's Originium resources.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Even if it's the only way to save Ursus.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Not the only way, apparently, in the eyes of many.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The generals of the empire wallow in the dream that my father weaved for them.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Wasn't enough blood shed on Bloodpeak already? Did they think it was a glorious defeat? Ursine territory would be twice as large now, if they were half the geniuses they think they are!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Absurd... Ridiculous!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...*cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Please, stay your anger, Majesty, as the doctor instructs.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I expect they understand these things full well. I believe they simply want to get as big a slice of Ursus's flesh, before chaos truly descends.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: For some of them, the unity of the nation and the plight of her people pale in comparison to ensuring their own prosperity and that of their descendants.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What are you implying?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I have news.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Out with it.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Only a few people with access to the Amber Palace know that Project Zero's energy utilization research is not progressing as hoped, all of whom are under strict surveillance.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: However, our intelligence indicates that the Fourth Army began moving almost at the same time that we received the news.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: They are quietly amassing forces for another push along the front lines, while simultaneously moving in the direction of First Army territory.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: They're ready on two fronts.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: What this means is that the Fourth Army has thoroughly infiltrated not only Grypherburg, but Tsarevgrad itself.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: This is a serious matter.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You wouldn't come to me with unfounded conjecture. Who do you suspect?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: (Hushed) Vasily Gorchikov.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The Vice Chairman? But isn't he the representative of the new aristocracy in the Duma—

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: But his family business has longstanding ties with military nobility, and the family of his late wife, House Gorchikov, is a noble house with a long and storied history.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: It was by marrying into his wife's family that he was recommended to the Imperial Guard.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Objectively speaking, Vasily's position was always uncertain.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I seem to recall that there was a servant in the Amber Palace from a branch of his family. Saveliy.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I see you catch my meaning.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: If someone in legislative leadership goes over to the pro-war faction—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Wait. Volkina, the honorary Vice Chairman who never attends meetings. She's a military noble too!

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: But she never expresses her opinion.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: It's her actions, not her words, that are important. The same goes for Vasily...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Keep a close eye on them. Do not let anyone get away. We must put a stop to any sign of a schism, whether superficial or material.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Understood...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...Are you tired, Witte?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Of course not... Majesty.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I'm beginning to feel powerless, Witte... can we really change anything? Is there anything we can do?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: There is still much we can do.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You have cast aside the shadow of your father. You must demonstrate to them that your kindness is not weakness, that it requires even greater strength.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: We must not surrender to the things that you rejected.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Enough... I do not want to hear such flattery, least of all from you.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The citizen's forum is a necessary reform. We need more people to stand with us. Time is short.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The empire cannot afford any more internal strife. We cannot use violence against these dissenters.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: More patience... continue to work to persuade them, try to awaken their love for this nation, or at the very least, a little bit of conscience...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You're right, Witte... we can't surrender yet.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...I should have come in the last time I passed by. It's totally different inside!

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Why didn't you?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Well, I thought I would do that when there's no longer a line of patients outside the door waiting for treatment.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Now it looks like they all fit inside, even if it does get a little crowded.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I heard you helped a lot.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Not nearly enough.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Do you know, there's a girl here, one of the surviving miners from the Far North who told me the entry hall was the first area to be completed. She likes it because it's always warm and bright, even at night.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: But I know that Rhodes Island had to invest in appearances first, just to satisfy the nobles and facilitate further operation.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Otherwise, they would hardly have paid attention to an Oripathy treatment center in downtown all of a sudden.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: It is warm and bright, though.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...Sometimes I wonder whether you're just acting dumb, or—

steps.name: Intermittent Voice
steps.text: ...think, it's important.

steps.name: Intermittent Voice
steps.text: But, should we wait...

steps.name: Intermittent Voice
steps.text: For Dur-nar to, come back?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Oh, that's the girl I was talking about.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Get everyone, indoors... warmer than, outside.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: As for where, to put...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Oh. I can help, to carry some—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Vetochki.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: —Oh!

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Sorry, did I scare you?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No, no! I just didn't, hear you...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You came again! Thank you!

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Just happened to pass by. I see the streets outside are empty, and the stoves have been taken away. Have the rooms been cleared? Enough furniture and equipment for everyone?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No, not yet. Some mattresses and, sheets have arrived, but not enough, and it's so, cold outside...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Better to have, everyone, in the hall.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Oh! At night, we'll try to, get everyone, a bed!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: There won't be, anyone in the, hall, when there are, inspections...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...Tsk.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Listen, Vetochki, we both know that the requirements for the treatment center to be perfectly clean and tidy aren't realistic.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Forget about those for now. Just let me know if you need anything. I'll do what I can—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: But you sent, the mattresses, and sheets, didn't you?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...What? But I haven't gotten the new supplies yet—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Who came?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: A man, wearing clothes, like yours... he brought, the things, and a few, people.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Just now...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: That's him!

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...Platon?

steps.name: Platon
steps.text: ...Tsk.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I thought you took leave to see your sick mother?

steps.name: Platon
steps.text: Yes, this is one of the charities that my mother sponsors. But I'm surprised you found the time to come to Odoyev and look after these commoners, busy as you are.

steps.name: Platon
steps.text: I thought His Imperial Majesty and your bright future were the only things on your mind.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No—

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: Get back.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Behind me, Vetochki.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Is that so? What a coincidence.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Since when did House Lunin become a sponsor of Rhodes Island? When my family is taking full responsibility for this matter?

steps.name: Platon
steps.text: ...Perhaps you should make sure a contract is exclusive before you sign it.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I could say the same to you.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What ARE you doing here, Platon? You have never had the slightest interest in commoners or charity.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Yet you've started doing these things all of a sudden, with a whole retinue of bodyguards... either you've suddenly discovered the goodness in your heart, or you're putting on a performance.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: But where are your cameras and lights, if you just want to take a few touching photos for the newspapers and intercity net?

steps.name: Platon
steps.text: None of your business. Do you want my sponsorship or not?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Of course. Every little bit counts. Next time, however, I suggest you go through official channels.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: After all, it's not just Oripathy patients here, but also a group of witnesses under His Imperial Majesty's protection... you don't want to be in the position of having to explain if anything happens to them, do you?

steps.name: Platon
steps.text: ...Hmph!

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Where are the supplies he brought, Vetochki?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: The blankets, have been, handed out... the mattresses are, still in the, warehouse.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: We're planning to, clear out, more rooms, then t-take the, mattresses out.
Eloysius scans the faces of the patients in the hall. They are draped in new blankets, some huddled together, others curled up on the floor.
No one wants to interrupt a moment like this.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Let me see the rest of the stuff.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: This is where the supplies he sent are stored.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Care to give a hand, Gospodin Hellagur? I would like to perform another check.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: You suspect him.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I didn't think you would be interested.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Not so much a suspicion as a hunch... but maybe it's just all the assassinations and talk of spies that's gotten me on edge.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: When you think about it, procuring this stuff represents no difficulty for his family whatsoever. It just never occurred to them to do so.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I'm supposed to be his superior, sort of, but I never managed to have a good influence on him—

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: My impression is that rank works differently in the Imperial Guard from the Armies.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Unlike the Armies, which have a strict promotion hierarchy, Imperial Guards mostly graduate directly from the military academy. As members of the aristocracy, all of you start as lieutenants.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: You are equal in rank, even if you hold different positions, and this will not change in the near future.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Are you saying it's normal that he resents me?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I've seen it many times. Besides, the Imperial Guard doesn't have automatic promotion by tenure.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Not to mention these are peaceful times, and not even the Great Rebellion could breach the walls of Grypherburg. There are few opportunities for merit and promotion.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: You're complaining.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Of course I'm not! Besides, things are changing. What I wouldn't give to not have the opportunity to earn merit now...

spans.text: Of course I'm not! Besides, things are changing. What I wouldn't give to
have the opportunity to earn merit now...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Platon's family has been trying to get him into the Central Army and onto the front lines. I rejected the reassignment. I suppose it's another reason why he doesn't like me.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: If things have gotten to the point when the Central Army is mobilized, no one in Grypherburg is immune.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The Capital Ursus Guard, part of the Central Army, must stand with the Imperial Guard as the final line of defense.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: It's disunity that you're concerned about.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You're much easier to talk to when you don't play dumb, you know? If the vice-chairman was here, he would tell me to stop wearing myself out and put myself and family first.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The Far North Incident has brought the schism amongst the factions of Grypherburg to the surface, while the insurrection in Katorga has raised the alarm for the fence-sitters.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I have no doubt that Grypherburg would have fallen apart in the literal sense of the word, if any of the recent assassination attempts had succeeded—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Wait, these supplies...

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Is something wrong?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: They're all military supplies. They're usually only seen in the military and the factories that supply it.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The council may occasionally divert military supplies in the event of an emergency, but Platon? How did he get his hands on these things?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What was he doing here?
Hmph... hah.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...Who's there?!

steps.name: Emperor's Blade
steps.text: Colluding with traitors under the pretense of an Infected treatment center. Just as I thought.

steps.name: Emperor's Blade
steps.text: Tell me, lieutenant.

steps.name: Emperor's Blade
steps.text: Where is the traitor?
